entries.title: Trump Signals Further Interest in Working With Democrats on ‘TrumpCare’
entries.summary: The president reposted a photo of Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s message promoting health care for “every American, from cradle to grave.”
entries.content:
President Donald Trump reposted incoming Michigan Senator Abdul El-Sayed’s mockups of a plan for “TrumpCare” gold cards on Saturday — the latest indication the president may be willing to work with the incoming Democratic majority on health care proposals.

El-Sayed, a Democrat whose midterms campaign centered on passing Medicare for All, uploaded on Nov. 12 pictures of a golden insurance card emblazoned with the word “TrumpCare” in a post directed to the president.

“Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave,” El-Sayed wrote.

Trump’s repost on Truth Social Saturday included no commentary.

Earlier Saturday, Trump told Fox News that Democrats “have some good points on health care.”

“There’s a chance we could get great health care, and a lot of other things, and we do it in a bipartisan way,” the president said. “There’s a very good chance — because otherwise, everything gets vetoed.”

On Friday, the president said Democrats had called him to discuss health care and immigration reform, similarly indicating he would work with the soon-to-be majority party, though he did not indicate with whom he had spoken.

El-Sayed’s Nov. 12 post was followed by a video the next week in which he called for passing “Trumpcare for All.”

“You want to be the most popular president in the history of America,” he said in the video, gesturing to a framed illustration of Trump as Jesus and a picture of the golden insurance card. “It’s really popular, people really want health care. You can put your name all over it. You can even give them a gold card.”

On Saturday, El-Sayed reiterated his openness to working with Trump and other Democratic senators to pass guaranteed health care.

“If the President is serious about meeting the unmet promise of guaranteed healthcare in this country, I’m ready to work alongside leaders in the Senate like Senators Van Hollen, Sanders, Wyden, and Warren to deliver,” El-Sayed said in a statement following Trump’s repost.

“President Trump, give me a call. I’m happy to chat," he said.
entries.author: Michelle Del Rey

entries.title: The Spirit Is Denied Its Championship Moment in a 2-1 Loss to the Current
entries.summary: Washington couldn't take advantage of its home field, falling in the NWSL final for a third straight year.
entries.content:
In a chippy, choppy NWSL championship match at Audi Field on Saturday, the Washington Spirit fell to the Kansas City Current, 2-1 — the franchise’s third consecutive loss in the league final.

"This one hurts way worse than any of the other ones," Spirit star Trinity Rodman said after the match. "I don’t even think you have words in this moment — it’s too fresh. But we’re all proud of each other. We’re all gonna be together no matter what."

Playing for a title in front of its home crowd for the first time in franchise history, Washington was forced into a physical game from the very start. Rodman went down early after a collision and briefly left the field, ultimately returning to play after a few minutes, albeit rather gingerly. Both teams struggled to find any sort of offensive rhythm. The clubs set a record for fouls in the first half of a championship game with 19, and they continued apace in the second.

“I don’t think that physicality is something new for them,” midfielder Andi Sullivan said of the Current. “It’s a very fine line of returning the favor.”

Kansas City's first goal came early in the second half on a corner kick from Vanessa DiBernardo. It was the second consecutive playoff game where the Spirit conceded an “Olimpico,” a goal straight off a corner kick, with no other players making contact with the ball. The Spirit had the possession advantage for much of the rest of the second half and created several big chances. Coach Adrián González pushed every button that he could with his substitution options, but nothing came through for the Spirit.

Most of the evening's drama came during a long and hectic period of stoppage time. Kansas City went up 2-0 on a counterattack that looked to be the dagger. But Washington responded shortly after, as Rodman headed in a goal that reignited the home crowd. In one final push, Washington launched a furious series of attacks until the final whistle. None prevailed.

"It obviously sucks to lose, but you got to give credit to Kansas," Rodman said. "They were very dominant, they were very together and they finished their chances. So you can’t be mad.”

The energy of a sold-out crowd was felt throughout the match, as the volume picked up at any scoring chance and boos rained down upon the referees late. Outside the stadium, the vibe was high as locals reflected on the journey that had led to this night.

“We used to play at a high school soccerplex in Maryland, now we sell out a 19,000-seat stadium, like, every week,” said Alison Cassady, a D.C. resident of 25 years and season ticket holder. “I love seeing it.”

Cassady was one of the many fans who walked to the game from The Wharf on Saturday afternoon. They marched alongside a live band that blared hits like “September” and “Livin' on a Prayer,” and led the crowd in chants.

They danced down Southwest D.C. streets, twirling flags and waving foam glowsticks that burned blue against the night sky. Many came with their young children — one determined mother even pushed her infant in a stroller.

As the hype train pulled up to Audi Field, the stadium was playing Beyoncé’s "Who Run the World (Girls)." This, fans hoped, would be their moment.

But hours later, it was the opponent and its fans who celebrated at the final whistle. Rodman, sitting on the pitch, put her hands to her face to cover a steady stream of tears as Current players formed a joyous huddle.

“It's heartbreaking,” fan Randall Marshall said after the loss. “I feel like, overall, we outplayed them. But sometimes that's the beautiful game, right? That one play, it just is not enough to lift the trophy.”
entries.author: Emma Baccellieri
